[LargeArrayBuilder.SizeOpt.cs#L20-L21](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/49a4893eed57f1de8734d21e4d8d3ab13e967c10/src/libraries/Common/src/System/Collections/Generic/LargeArrayBuilder.SizeOpt.cs#L20-L21) 
Should the constructor here be removed entirely? I'm not so sure as it looks like it could be removed completely even before C# 10.

review_comments: ❔ Considering `_builder = default` is the same behavior, is there any reason why we want this form?

I chose it that way as it is _SizeOpt_ and `this = default` has code size _8_ whilst `_builder = default` has code size 13 in IL (according [sharplab](https://sharplab.io/#v2:)) and thought it matters for the _size_. Machine code is the same in both variants.
And (minor) iif in the future any field gets added the build is fine.

On the other hand with
```suggestion
        public LargeArrayBuilder() => _builder = default;
```
(as you suggested) it is more explicit.
is there any functional or perf difference between assignment like this vs `: this()`? If not, I personally find old syntax clearer, do we change entire code base with this?

With a struct, default and new() are identical if the struct doesn't define a parameterless ctor, and until C# 10 you couldn't. If the struct does define one,  default and new() are different: the latter invokes the ctor, the former doesn't. Our style has been to use default to make it clear no ctor is being invoked. Now that you can define ctors, I think it makes even more sense to keep that style and reserve new() for when a ctor invoke is needed. But we'll need analyzer assistance.
Oh,  I just realized you meant this = default vs a this ctor delegation. Similar answer: it depends on whether a ctor is defined as to whether or zero initializes or invokes a ctor.
